questions.question: When checking power steering fluid during a vehicle inspection, which task is NOT required?

options.text: Point out where the power steering fluid dipstick is located.
Check that there is enough power steering fluid.
Make sure the power steering fluid level is above the full mark.
Make sure the power steering fluid level is above the refill mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the power steering fluid level is above the full mark.
questions.explanation: When checking power steering fluid during an inspection, you must show where the dipstick is and confirm there is enough fluid. The fluid level only needs to be above the refill mark, not the full mark.

questions.question: Bent lock rings are:

options.text: Not a problem in dry weather.

questions.explanation: Bent, cracked, or mismatched lock rings are dangerous and should never be used.

questions.question: On a wet road, reduce your speed by:
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed when roads are wet because they have less grip. Slow down by about one-third of your normal speed.

questions.question: When stopping a manual transmission vehicle, you should:

options.text: Push in the clutch when the engine is nearly at idle.
Release the clutch when the engine is nearly at idle.
Shift into neutral when the engine is nearly at idle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push in the clutch when the engine is nearly at idle.
questions.explanation: When stopping, press the brake pedal gently and stop smoothly. For a manual transmission vehicle, push in the clutch when the engine is nearly at idle.

questions.question: A bus driver does NOT need to stop at:
questions.explanation: Bus drivers must stop 15 to 50 feet before railroad crossings to look and listen for trains. You do not need to stop at streetcar crossings, when a police officer is directing traffic, when you have a green light, or at crossings marked "exempt" or "abandoned."

questions.question: Cargo in a trailer must be:

options.text: Stacked no higher than three feet.
Secured so it does not move during transport.
Loaded with heavy items on top of light items.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secured so it does not move during transport.
questions.explanation: Cargo must be properly secured to prevent movement. Loose cargo is dangerous to the driver and other road users.

questions.question: Rust around wheel nuts may indicate:
questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts suggests they may be loose. Check and tighten the nuts if you see rust in that area.

questions.question: Texting while driving is:

options.text: Allowed if you are contacting your employer.

questions.explanation: Texting while driving is dangerous and never permitted when operating a commercial vehicle.

questions.question: When inspecting a power steering vehicle, make sure that:

options.text: The fluid is at the correct level.
The hoses are connected to the battery.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fluid is at the correct level.
questions.explanation: Check the hoses, pumps, and fluid level in power steering systems. Look for and fix any leaks before driving.

questions.question: An example of required emergency equipment is:

options.text: A spare supply of electrical fuses.

questions.correctAnswerText: A spare supply of electrical fuses.
questions.explanation: Required emergency equipment includes: at least one fire extinguisher; spare electrical fuses (unless the vehicle has circuit breakers); and warning devices for parked vehicles like reflective triangles.

questions.question: How should you drive a heavy vehicle to avoid interfering with traffic?

options.text: Pass other vehicles while going uphill.
Use your brakes while going downhill.

questions.explanation: If your vehicle is too heavy to match traffic speed, stay in the right lane when possible.

questions.question: After passengers board, what should a driver do before starting to drive?

options.text: Give passengers time to sit down or hold on.
Honk the horn and enter traffic right away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give passengers time to sit down or hold on.
questions.explanation: Always start and stop smoothly to keep passengers safe. Wait for all passengers to be seated or braced before you begin driving.

questions.question: What should you NOT find when checking your tires?

options.text: Tire tread that is 4/32 of an inch deep.

questions.explanation: Front tires need at least 4/32 inch of tread. Other tires need at least 2/32 inch. Valve stems must not be cut or cracked. All tires must be the same size.

questions.question: How do bridges usually freeze compared to other road surfaces?

options.text: Only when the temperature drops well below 32 degrees Fahrenheit.
They have heaters that prevent freezing.

questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before regular roads. Drive carefully on bridges when the temperature is near freezing.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a suspension system defect?

options.text: Missing or broken leaves in the spring.

questions.explanation: Suspension defects include cracked or broken spring hangers, missing or broken spring leaves, and leaking shock absorbers. Have these fixed right away. Cracked lights are not a suspension problem.

questions.question: What should you do if you feel sleepy while driving?

options.text: Continue driving to finish the trip.
Drive faster to get to your destination sooner.
Pull over and take a nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and take a nap.
questions.explanation: The only safe option is to stop driving and sleep. Fighting fatigue is dangerous and causes many fatal crashes. Energy pills may keep you awake but will not make you more alert. When they wear off, you will be even more tired.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a vehicle inspection report?

options.text: Tell the company about problems that need to be fixed.
Make sure the vehicle is checked regularly.
Hold people responsible for checking the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the company about problems that need to be fixed.
questions.explanation: A vehicle inspection report lets the company know about any problems that need repair.

questions.question: What does blocking cargo do?

options.text: Should only be done in bad weather.

questions.explanation: Blocking keeps cargo from moving around while the vehicle is in motion.

questions.question: Which of the following is acceptable during a pre-trip tire inspection?
questions.explanation: Check your tires carefully before driving. Tire sizes must match. Tires must not be cut, cracked, or damaged.

questions.question: How long does it take for engine oil pressure to reach normal after starting?
questions.explanation: Oil pressure should reach normal within seconds of starting the engine. Do not drive if oil pressure is too low.
